title: Salivary cortisol assessment among individuals with idiopathic hypersomnia to exclude HPA axis dysfunction
summary:
Idiopathic hypersomnia is a neurological disorder that affects the sleep-wake cycle, and its cause is currently unknown.  It is characterized by pronounced morning sleepiness and an excessive need for daytime sleep despite prolonged nocturnal sleep. This condition has a significant negative impact on the quality of life of those affected.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether affected individuals may have an underactive adrenal cortex that produces insufficient hormones. These hormones play an important role in metabolism, stress response, and the regulation of the sleep-wake cycle. In this study, saliva tests will be used to measure hormone levels, including cortisol, a hormone that helps regulate the sleep-wake rhythm.
Should an association between adrenal dysfunction and idiopathic hypersomnia be demonstrated, the results could contribute to the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Patients diagnosed with idiopathic hypersomnia in a sleep laboratory (exclusion criteria must not apply)
2) Healthy control group (exclusion criteria must not apply here either)
Exclusion criteria:
• Treatment for depression (with medication or psychotherapy) in the last twelve months
• Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus
• Use of glucocorticoid medication in the last month
• Moderate or severe obstructive sleep apnea syndrome
